- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually underestimates later days.
- Forecasts show a persistent upward bias relative to true values, particularly in the middle to late portion of the 30-day window.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+), model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct, but often lags the true price correction by 3–5 days.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion toward lower levels after sustained high prices; true values often dip significantly after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and underestimate the magnitude of downward corrections.
- Model exhibits a “lagged” response to recent price drops — it takes 3–5 days to adjust downward, while true values react faster.
- Forecasts show a strong tendency to follow a smooth, linear trend, ignoring volatility and sudden price reversals.
- Model underestimates the depth of price corrections after spikes, especially in the 10–20 day range.
- Forecasts are overly confident in upward momentum, even when historical data shows signs of mean reversion or downward pressure.
